look_here_first: FLORIDA PASPALUM — trace a robust leafy stem to its COMPLETE terminal head, often 2–5 long spikelet-bearing racemes attached at different points. On each one-sided raceme look for large, smooth, fairly rounded flattened paired 'coins'; measure actual mature spikelets (~3.5–4.2 mm in the UT Texas treatment) against a 1-mm scale. For sterile plants check the ACTUAL 1.2–3.3 mm brown membranous ligule at the blade–sheath junction and short stout rhizomatous crown, unlike switchgrass's hair-fringe ligule and Indiangrass's claw/auricled collar. No current target-species photo proves the membrane or separate glumes; keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.

crew_field_steps: Recognize and photograph the sizeable erect broad-leaved bunch; current photo shows the leafy habit only.
Find a mature flowering head with multiple long one-sided racemes; count branches on a SINGLE culm and show complete axis.
Measure and photograph the relatively broad rounded oval spikelets with a mm ruler, and check leaf blade/sheath ligule before separating from dallisgrass and P. pubiflorum.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full flowering culm from base to complete mature seedhead.
Two mature racemes photographed from side and face with scale.
Broad oval mature spikelets plus glume/hair macro at mm scale.
Leaf sheath/collar membrane and vegetative habit paired with P. dilatatum.

field_photo_learning_steps: 1. Photograph an intact plant from soil/crown to flowering tip. The existing Commons image gives a stout clump view, but not a physically traced same-stem collar and seedhead.

2. Photograph the entire flowering architecture side-on: normally 2–5 one-sided slender racemes, each borne at its own point on the main axis; do not confuse the single branch with the entire seedhead.

3. Examine ONE actual raceme: rounded/obovate, often paired, one-sided flattened spikelets in rows. Mature fruit ~3.5–4.2 mm under the UT Austin Texas treatment; take 5 separate measurements rather than guessing from a photo.

4. Gently pull back a FULL-SIZE mature leaf blade exactly where it leaves the sheath: look for a short brown MEMBRANOUS ligule ~1.2–3.3 mm, not just a fringe of hairs. Capture the tuft of long hairs above it in a separate angle.

5. Compare vegetative big bluestem: a tall, leafy grass can resemble Florida paspalum from a distance, but big bluestem has a different shorter collar and its terminal few thick turkey-foot racemes bear Andropogoneae spikelets.

6. Compare the different-species pubiflorum photo of smaller (~2.7–3.2 mm) oval spikelets and Dallisgrass's potentially hair-fringed glumes; don't substitute image-specimen scale or source determination.

7. Microscope: photograph one full P. floridanum spikelet flat and convex side with a scale, then separate the upper glume, sterile lower lemma and leathery fertile lemma/palea. Paspalum has a suppressed or absent lower glume; do not invent one.
8. Teach-back: can a crew member correctly point to an entire raceme, two separate attached spikelets and the TRUE blade-sheath ligule on the SAME collected plant? If not, field label provisional.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Paspalum: what to inspect
steps: LOOK at actual Florida paspalum habit (gallery image 0). This source-reported clump image is real but not diagnostic without the head.

LOOK at the already physically archived David J. Stang Paspalum floridanum flowering head (canonical image index 2, now featured after habit). Follow three one-sided racemes and their attached rounded green spikelets; no millimeter scale or dissected glumes are shown.
Check smaller pubiflorum photographed spikelets vs Florida's larger published 3.5–4.2 mm mature ones; measure one real species candidate at 1-mm scale.
Photograph true lifted blade/sheath junction to show brown membranous ligule 1.2–3.3 mm plus basal hairs; OTHER SPECIES Dallisgrass photo shows WHERE but NOT P. floridanum anatomy.
Record exact full raceme, paired spikelets and reconstructed fertile/sterile bracts from the SAME specimen before any 100% diagnosis.

P. pubiflorum commonly has smaller 2.7–3.2 mm spikelets, and pubescence needs careful comparison.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.look_here_first: Stout rhizomatous perennial with 2–5(–6) one-sided racemes on a complete stem; find paired broad rounded 'coin' spikelets. Confirm large 3.5–4.2 mm mature spikelets and a true membranous ligule, not just flowering-head silhouette.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.growth_form: Perennial bunch with short horizontal rhizomes, stout culms; Williamson County treatment plants around 100–140 cm flowering. Rooted crown needed for confirmation.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.ligule_collar: Williamson County ligule a 1.5–2.5 mm membranous, jagged-edged flap; collar 2–3 mm with hairs to 8 mm. Do not mistake collar hairs for the membrane.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.spikelet_glume_lemma_awn: Spikelets 3.5–4.2 × 2.8–3.2 mm, usually paired along one-sided racemes. Lower glume ABSENT; upper glume 3.5–4 mm, five-veined; lower sterile lemma subequal to upper glume, no lower palea; upper fertile lemma approximately 3 × 2.6 mm, tough and enclosing a two-veined palea approximately 3 × 2 mm. Awns absent.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.local_lookalikes: P. pubiflorum usually smaller mature spikelets (about 2.7–3.2 mm); P. dilatatum has distinctive long silky upper-glume margins; P. urvillei usually has more racemes and smaller spikelets. Count and measure actual structures, not stature alone.

field_id_short_tiles.short: Few long racemes with broad paired 'coins'
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace ONE entire mature flowering culm: Florida paspalum usually bears about 2–5 one-sided racemes attached at different points along the axis. Panels 0–2 show species-labelled habit and flowering branches. Find broad rounded paired flattened spikelets, but do not identify from leaf width, height or a single raceme photograph alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROSS FIELD CUE VISIBLE; SAME-PLANT ROOT-TO-HEAD PHOTO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · CHECK THE RHIZOME AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Short stout rhizomes; real membrane, not hairs
field_id_short_tiles.details: A robust perennial with short rhizomes. Open the INNER blade/sheath junction to expose the true membranous ligule: Williamson County treatment gives approximately 1.5–2.5 mm, while USGS describes about 1.2–3.3 mm. Nearby collar/sheath hairs are separate. Panel 5 shows a DALLISGRASS collar (different species) for location only, NOT evidence of Florida paspalum's ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — ROOTED CROWN AND MEASURED TRUE MEMBRANE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE PAIRED MATURE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.details: On one actual unilateral raceme, locate adjacent paired dorsally compressed oval spikelets. The UT Williamson County treatment gives mature spikelets approximately 3.5–4.2 × 2.8–3.2 mm. Measure several at 1-mm scale and photograph flat face plus edge; the current species photos do not prove these dimensions.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · SEPARATE GLUME, LEMMAS AND PALEA
field_id_short_tiles.short: No lower glume; upper glume ~3.5–4 mm
field_id_short_tiles.details: A true LOWER GLUME is absent. The upper glume is approximately 3.5–4 mm and five-veined; the lower sterile lemma is roughly its length, while the hard upper fertile lemma is about 3 × 2.6 mm and encloses a palea. There are no long projecting awns. Do not label the adjacent PAIR of spikelets as two florets, or invent a missing lower glume. These parts require a ripe dissection.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE LOCAL PASPALUM LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 3 is DALLISGRASS (P. dilatatum), not Florida paspalum: compare its long silky upper-glume hairs and typically more numerous narrower spikelets. Panel 4 is HAIRYSEED PASPALUM (P. pubiflorum), often with smaller ~2.7–3.2 mm mature spikelets. Vaseygrass (P. urvillei) often has many more racemes and smaller spikelets. Branch counts and spikelet sizes overlap; use actual measured same-maturity anatomy.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE PHOTOS LABELLED; MATCHED MATURE MACROS MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · REQUIRE PHOTO AND SITE PROOF
field_id_short_tiles.short: One rooted plant, collar and dissected spikelet
field_id_short_tiles.details: Before marking FINISHED, obtain a voucher-confirmed local plant linking crown, true 1–3 mm membranous ligule, full head and 3.5–4.2 mm paired mature spikelets. Dissect upper glume, sterile lemma, hard fertile lemma and palea under a calibrated macro. Check public reuse for each archived JPEG and every arrow against actual visible pixels; existing comparison photos must remain correctly labelled. Preserve taxonomy and nativity holds.
